title: Governing democracy, the internet, and boardrooms

reader_summary.headline: 2024 is an important year for democracy.
reader_summary.overview: 2024 is an important year for democracy. This year, over 60 countries have and will head to the polls, representing just about half of the global population. But governance extends past the leaders of nation states. In fact, as the revenue of some companies dwarf the economies of some nations.

key_points.text: In fact, as the revenue of some companies dwarf the economies of some nations.
key_points.evidence_quote: In fact, as the revenue of some companies dwarf the economies of some nations, the way these entities govern themselves is both more interesting and more important than ever.

key_points.text: I'm Robert Hackett, and today we have a special episode about governance in many forms, from nation states to corporate boards.
key_points.evidence_quote: I'm Robert Hackett, and today we have a special episode about governance in many forms, from nation states to corporate boards, to internet services and beyond.

thesis: The episode explores various models for internet governance, ranging from corporate self-regulation and collective self-regulation among platforms to hybrid structures like oversight boards and benefit trusts. It highlights that corporations are already subject to extensive state, national, and international laws, while the current era is defined by a lack of Supreme Court doctrine on social media rights and ongoing debates about the extent of government regulation versus platform autonomy.
